title: Reefer Cargo Services: one live service per reefer container of a booking
content:
## Scope

This rule of **Reefer Cargo Services** governs how many reefer services may exist when a reefer service is ordered for a container of a reefer booking. It applies to every tier, from AHL Reefer Standard to AHL Reefer Superfreezer.

## Rule

1. A customer may hold any number of reefer services. There is no limit on the number of reefer services per customer.
2. Each reefer container of a booking has at most one live service. A service is live when its status is anything other than cancelled, that is, when it is requested, PTI passed, plugged in, in transit, delivered or closed.
3. The check is made against the company's own service records before the new service is ordered, matching the booking and the container number of the new order against the existing services on that same booking and container.

## Input, judgement, result

| Existing service on the same booking and container | Judgement | Result for a new order on that container |
|---|---|---|
| None | No live service exists | This rule does not stand in the way |
| One with status requested, PTI passed, plugged in, in transit, delivered or closed | A live service already exists | The new service is not ordered |
| Only services with status cancelled | Cancelled services are not live | This rule does not stand in the way |

## Points of judgement

**Does a customer with many reefer services on other bookings face a limit?** No. The number of services per customer is unlimited; the restriction is per container of a booking.

**The same container number appears on two different bookings. Is that one container twice?** The rule counts live services per booking and container together. A live service on one booking does not count against the same container number on a different booking.

**Does a closed service still block a new order on the same booking and container?** Yes. Closed is not cancelled, so a closed service remains live for this rule.

## Hypothetical illustration

> Hypothetical: a booking carries three reefer containers. Containers one and two each have a service in transit; container three had a service that was cancelled. A new service may be considered for container three under this rule, while a second service for container one or two is not ordered.
